manifest.name: dsh-ntr-plus
manifest.description: Interactive Agent Client Protocol (ACP) client for the DSH web UI: attach any ACP-capable agent and stream its session.

scripts.prepack: npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build

bundle.text:
# Mount line for the dsh-ntr-plus bundle.
#
# The pure package-name row is REQUIRED for the ClientModuleRegistry to match
# the browser half (dsh.client in package.json); the host half is the same row
# (one plugin module carries both Node and browser entries).
#
# `agents` below SEEDS the agent registry at boot (BridgeManager's constructor
# `defs`), but it is not the only source and not a boundary. The settings page's
# launch-command box (`AgentForm.commandLine` in src/client/panel.tsx) writes
# through RPC `agent/save` → `validateAgentDef` → `BridgeManager.saveAgent` into
# `~/.dsh/dsh-ntr-plus/agents.json`, and that is what spawns the child.
# `validateAgentDef` checks shape only (non-empty, splittable command line,
# length) — there is no program whitelist, so the browser CAN name any program.
# A child's env comes from the same two places, and `detectHostAgents` hands the
# stored `command` / `args` / `env` back to the browser UNSANITIZED as
# `currentConfig`, where `envRows` edits them.
- insert:
    - id: dsh-ntr-plus
      name: dsh-ntr-plus
      config:
        agents: []
        # transcriptMaxEntries: 600
        # probeModelsOnBoot: true   # DEAD — validated and stored, never read.
        #                                `bootstrapCatalogs` is empty, so boot
        #                                probes nothing whatever this says; true
        #                                and false behave identically. Real
        #                                probes: RPC `agent/probe-models` (the
        #                                settings button) and `probeAgentModels`
        #                                after `saveAgent`.
        # Reliability tuning (defaults shown):
        # startupTimeoutMs: 60000    # budget for initialize / session/new / session/load
        # permissionTimeoutMs: 0     # auto-cancel a pending approval after N ms. 0 waits
        #                                for the human on the DESIGNED ledger path; on a
        #                                DEGRADED native route the turn still ends, after
        #                                `permissionFallbackTimeoutMs` (default 300000) —
        #                                see `LedgerFallbackReason`.
        # nativeApprovalTimeoutMs: 300000
        #                              How long the native approval route (the composer
        #                              takeover) may stay unanswered before the ask is
        #                              WITHDRAWN and re-asked on the settings ledger. 0 waits
        #                              for the host forever. Default matches
        #                              `permissionFallbackTimeoutMs`: one window for "this
        #                              route is not working", not two. Raise it if a
        #                              deployment's users routinely deliberate for minutes
        #                              before answering (withdrawing only relocates the
        #                              question to Settings — it never answers for them).
        # permissionFallbackTimeoutMs: 300000
        #                              Deadline for a DEGRADED ask (`unavailable`, or
        #                              `native-timeout` after the withdrawal above): past it
        #                              the ask is answered `cancelled` instead of hanging the
        #                              turn. 0 disables even this. `permissionTimeoutMs > 0`
        #                              governs every path alike and overrides both.
        #                              `nativeApprovalTimeoutMs` and
        #                              `permissionFallbackTimeoutMs` are ALSO editable at
        #                              runtime (NTR 设置 → 审批时限). The card's value is
        #                              persisted in the plugin's own state file and OUTRANKS
        #                              this file; the card shows what this file asked for and
        #                              offers a reset back to it. Only `permissionTimeoutMs`
        #                              stays config-file-only, as the override of both.
        # cancelFallbackMs: 15000    # force-finalize a turn the agent ignores after session/cancel (0 = off)
        # staleCancelRetryDelayMs: 600  # resend a prompt answered cancelled with no cancel requested (0 = at once)
        # staleCancelMaxRetries: 2      # cap on those resends before the cancelled stop is reported as-is
        # ACP 模式 (agent preset) is declared by this package's own bundle
        # patch list (package.json `dsh.bundle.patch` → presets/acp/acp.patch.yml),
        # so it needs no install step and has no config knob. The settings card
        # only reports the harness roster's verdict for the `preset-acp` row.
        # The plugin's OWN default ACP agent (panel's ★ button) lives in the
        # agent registry file at `~/.dsh/dsh-ntr-plus/agents.json`, key
        # `defaultAgentId` (`pluginStateDir` + `BridgeManager.getStoragePath`).
        # `~/.dsh/acp-agents.json` is only a MIGRATION SOURCE (`legacyStatePaths`):
        # `migrateLegacyState` moves it into the plugin directory on first boot,
        # and nothing writes the old path afterwards.
        # This plugin never reads or writes DSH's deployment default model: no
        # ACP route is ever written there, so there is nothing to guard. (An
        # older revision did write one and needed a host-side guard to put a
        # native route back — both are gone; see AGENTS.md constraint 22.)
        # Per-agent ACP-model filter — which of the agent's models its own
        # conversation seats offer (panel checkboxes persist here). ACP models
        # are never advertised in DSH's model catalog, so they cannot leak into
        # a non-ACP conversation:
        # agents:
        #   - id: pi
        #     command: pi-acp
        #     npmPackage: pi-acp        # auto `npm install -g` when command is missing from PATH
        #     exposedModels: [model-a, model-b]   # opt-in `agent@choice` variants; unset/[] = base entry only
        #     idleTimeoutMs: 1800000     # release a chat process once it has been idle
        #                                #   this long (ms) with NO live session
        #                                #   (0 = never; unset = 30 min). This window
        #                                #   applies ONLY to a process that has hosted a
        #                                #   session: a probe child (`everHostedSession`
        #                                #   false — what a model probe or a post-save
        #                                #   probe leaves behind, i.e. the row the panel
        #                                #   shows as connected) is released after
        #                                #   `probeIdleTimeoutMs` (5 min) whatever this
        #                                #   says, 0 included.
        #     mcpServers:                # extra MCP servers handed to the agent at
        #       - name: codegraph        #   session setup (the agent starts them
        #         transport: stdio       #   itself). The plugin's OWN shape: every
        #         command: /opt/bin/codegraph   #   entry carries a name and a transport.
        #         args: [serve, --mcp]    #   `stdio` needs command, `http`/`sse` need
        #         env: { KEY: value }    #   url. NOT the ACP wire shape, whose stdio
        #                                #   variant has no `type` field (an entry
        #                                #   written that way is silently dropped by
        #                                #   the agent).

# The `acp` agent preset — "NTR 模式": a session whose conversation is served by
# an external ACP agent (dsh-ntr-plus's `acp` LLM provider) instead of a
# harness-driven model.
#
# WHY THIS FILE (and not a directory under `~/.dsh/.agent-presets/`): agent
# presets are declarations carried by the patches of the profile's selected
# bundles (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset`'s `preset-<id>` row). The legacy
# `$DSH_HOME/.agent-presets/<id>/` directory — `preset.yml` + `agent.cordis.yml`
# — is dead: nothing reads it any more, so a preset that only exists there never
# reaches the roster. dsh-ntr-plus is itself a profile bundle (`dsh.bundle.patch` in
# package.json), so declaring the preset here is what makes "NTR 模式" appear in
# the mode chooser with no copying step at all.
#
# WHY THE PRESET EXISTS: an ACP agent is ANOTHER agent reached over the wire, and
# the harness is only its shell. Everything the harness normally contributes to a
# session's model view — its identity, the deployment persona, tool schemas, the
# AGENTS.md digest, the skill catalog, the runtime-context snapshot, plan mode,
# compaction — describes work the DSH loop would have done itself. None of it
# reaches the ACP agent (dsh-ntr-plus forwards only the person's own message — see
# AGENTS.md rule 16) and all of it perturbs the conversation, so this composition
# contributes none of it. The model-visible surface is the ACP agent's own.
#
# This is an AGENT-PLANE composition, mounted once per process under a standing
# scope; every session joined to it shares these two rows. It publishes no
# service, so it needs no `isolate` realm.
#
# Deliberately absent — do not add these back without a reason:
#   - `tool-*` rows: the agent's tools live in its own process. Advertising DSH
#     tools would be dead weight (the bridge never emits a DSH tool call), and
#     the agent's own tool calls are not DSH tool calls.
#   - `agent-instructions`: AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md digests are harness context.
#   - `tool-skill` / `skill-filesystem`: same, plus the `<available_skills>` dump.
#   - `plan-mode` / `tool-todo` / `tool-goal`: harness state machines this
#     session never enters — the agent brings its own modes (the composer
#     control in dsh-ntr-plus drives those).
#   - `compaction-basic` / `command-compact`: a compaction would dispatch an
#     auxiliary harness call on the ACP route; the agent owns its own context.
#   - the delegation/workflow rows: delegation is a harness capability.
- insert:
    - id: preset-acp
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset'
      config:
        # `id` is what a session stores and what the browser half matches
        # (`ACP_PRESET_ID` in src/client/acp-ui.tsx — keep the two in sync).
        id: acp
        name: NTR 模式
        description: 会话由外接 Agent 驱动（Agent Client Protocol）：宿主不提供工具、提示词、项目指令与运行上下文，原生聊天只作外壳。
        order: 6
        plugins:
          # `complete: true` makes this the whole system prompt — it suppresses
          # the static harness identity and the deployment persona.
          # `includeRuntimeContext: false` suppresses the dynamic runtime-context
          # snapshot, which the driver would otherwise append as a sourced user
          # message right behind the person's own message (the bridge filters
          # those by source as well; this row is why they are not even
          # assembled).
          - id: persona
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
            config:
              prefix: >-
                This session's conversation is served by an external ACP agent
                over the Agent Client Protocol. The harness provides no tools
                and no context of its own: the agent's own instructions, tools,
                and modes are authoritative.
              complete: true
              includeRuntimeContext: false

          # Belt and braces for the contract above: strip harness context
          # injections from every proposed step, so a row added here later (or a
          # host-plane plugin injecting one) cannot quietly re-enter the
          # session's model view either.
          #
          # The guard is a file of THIS package (`presets/acp/acp-guard.mjs`,
          # exported as `dsh-ntr-plus/acp-guard`). A relative `./acp-guard.mjs` would
          # not resolve here: a preset declaration's plugin names resolve against
          # the declaring Loader's resolution base (the profile directory), not
          # against the patch file that inserted the row.
          - id: acp-guard
            name: dsh-ntr-plus/acp-guard

readme.text:
> 这是 **GDWhisper/dsh-ntr 0.1.5 的个人构建版**（上游已到 0.3.x，机制改动很大，见 [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md)）。原项目 MIT，版权归 GDWhisper。

[English](./README.en.md) | 简体中文

在 [DSH（DeepSeek Harness）](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的网页/桌面端里，用你习惯的界面，直接和任意一个 **ACP agent**（CodeBuddy、Pi、Oh My Pi、Claude Code、OpenCode、Qoder 等）对话。

**DSH 提供界面，agent 提供能力。** 会话列表、输入框、侧栏、消息展示全部来自 DSH；推理、工具执行、文件读写、权限判断全部由你自己配置的那个 agent 完成，它跑在独立进程里，完全自治。这个插件只做一件事：把两边接通，并把 agent 的输出原样画到 DSH 的界面上。

> 模型选择、思考等级、工作模式都是 **agent 自己的概念**，不是 DSH 的模型目录。插件不替你换模型，也不会把 agent 的选择写进 DSH 的全局设置。

---

**NTR = Negotiated Target Routing（协商式目标路由）**。

一句话：你的宿主 Agent 作为 ACP 客户端，和目标 Agent 协商能力与权限，把这一轮任务交给它执行。

---

> **本发行包已内置构建产物 `lib/`**，下载即用，安装步骤见 [INSTALL.md](./INSTALL.md)（`dsh plugin --profile <name> add ./dsh-ntr-plus-0.1.6.tgz`）。
> 下文「从源码安装」描述的是上游仓库的开发流程，需要 `tsconfig.json` 与 `tests/`，这两项不在本包内。

本包面向 **DSH 0.1.5-rc ~ 0.2.x** 的插件 API（浏览器侧依赖 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-*@0.1.5-rc.1`）。上游 0.3.x 改过权限管线与模型目录机制，**不保证兼容**——装到 0.3.x 上可能加载失败、或设置页/模型分组出现但功能不生效。

装完自检两步：

1. **设置 → NTR** 能看到 agent 列表与「测试」按钮 → 宿主端已加载；
2. 输入框行尾的模型名点开，出现 `ACP` 分组 → 模型目录对接生效。

两步任一不成立，先确认 DSH 版本，再确认 `--profile` 没写错、装完已重启。

本插件是一个 DSH **bundle**：`package.json` 的 `dsh.bundle.patch` 声明了随包分发的两层补丁——插件本体的 `cordis.patch.yml`，与 NTR 模式 preset 的 `presets/acp/acp.patch.yml`。用 `dsh plugin` 安装后，包会加入 profile 的 `dsh.profile.bundles`，补丁层**自动生效**，无需手动编辑任何配置文件。

readme.section: 方式一：从 GitHub 安装（推荐）
readme.text:
```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:Feiyu180/dsh-ntr-plus
```

`--profile` 必填（网页版 `web`、桌面版 `desktop`、TUI `tui`），装完重启 DSH。

readme.section: 方式二：用发行包离线安装
readme.text:
下载 Release 里的 `dsh-ntr-plus-0.1.6.tgz`，然后：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-ntr-plus-0.1.6.tgz
```

本包已带构建产物 `lib/`，一般不需要自己构建；要改源码请走上游仓库的流程（本包不含 `tsconfig.json` / `tests/`）。

> `dsh plugin` 是 pnpm 转发器，`--profile <name>` 必填；官方桌面 App 的 profile 由它自己的插件管理器掌管，不要对着它的 profile 跑命令行。

1. 一个已经装好的 DSH（Web 或桌面版）。
2. 至少一个 ACP agent 的命令行程序。插件内置了几个常见预设，也可以填任何支持 stdio 的 ACP agent。

1. 打开 **设置 → NTR**。
2. 在「Agent 列表」里选一个预设一键填入，或点「从零新建自定义 Agent」手填启动命令。
3. 点「测试」。成功会显示 agent 的名字和握手耗时；失败会显示可操作的错误和 stderr 尾部。

保存后，这个 agent 就出现在输入框行尾的 NTR 底座里。

1. 新建一个会话，在模式选择里选「**NTR 模式**」。
2. 在输入框行尾的 NTR 底座里选一个 agent。
3. 直接说话。

agent 的回复和思考显示在主聊天区。工具活动按发生顺序插在它们中间：一行 `🛠️ **工具名** · 参数`，输出跟一个代码块。想看完整的工具输出、计划和 diff，切到对话头部的 **NTR** 标签页。

---

点一下，选哪个 agent 服务这条会话。这个菜单里只有 agent 列表——一个控件一件事。agent 自己的模型和思考等级是同一行里各自独立的芯片，各开各的菜单；如果 agent 还发布了额外配置项（温度、供应商开关等），模型芯片左边会多一个「高级」底座，点开逐项设置。首轮之前 agent 底座固定在行尾最右侧；锁定后它退场，模型和思考等级接管右端。那些清单由 agent 自己上报，不是你熟悉的 DSH 模型列表。

底座只出现在 **NTR 模式**的会话里。普通会话里看到的是 DSH 原生的模型选择器。

**一个会话一个 agent。** 首条消息发出前，底座一直在，你可以先选好、也可以反悔改选。首轮**开始**时会话就**锁定**在这个 agent 上：底座粉碎，名字变成**输入框卡片上边缘的小挂牌**（`NTR · <agent>`，骑在顶边上），挂牌只显示、不能点击——换 agent 请新建会话。模型、思考等级和「高级」芯片留在原位，它们属于同一个 agent，不涉及上下文迁移。如果首轮还没产生任何可见输出就失败/取消，锁定会自动回滚，底座回来，可以直接重选。

在 NTR 会话里输入 `/`，弹出的是 **agent 自己的命令清单**——它通过 ACP 声明的那些（例如 `compact`、`session`、`model`），不是 DSH 的命令。选中一项只是把命令名填进输入框；回车后整行原样发给 agent，由它执行。清单在**第一条消息之前**就能用：宿主记住了这个 agent 上次会话声明的命令（从没跑过的 agent 要等第一轮之后才有）。

DSH 自己的 `/model`、`/permission`、`/export` 等在这一模式下**不会**被宿主截走：同名命令也交给 agent，宿主命令菜单与技能补全不会出现。普通会话的斜杠行为完全不变。

readme.section: 审批与 agent 自己的权限模式
readme.text:
agent 要动敏感的东西时会问你。审批卡直接出现在聊天输入框里，你点允许或拒绝，它照着做。

每个 agent 问法不一样：有的给一组选项，有的只给允许/拒绝，有的会附上它要执行的具体命令。插件把这些原样呈现给你，不预先替你决定。

**权限模式由 agent 自己定义。** 每个 agent 在输入框工具行给出它自己的模式清单（例如 `Always Ask`、`Accept Edits`、`Plan`、`Bypass Permissions`），选项文字就是 agent 下发的原文。你切换模式，agent 就按新模式决定什么时候来问你。插件不另设一套权限档，也不替你翻译这些模式名。

> **注意**：DSH 自己的「访问模式」（只读 / 工作区写入 / 完全权限）管不到外部 agent。那个 agent 在自己的进程里，DSH 的文件沙箱对它没有作用力。真正生效的是 agent 自己的权限模式，以及它向你发起的那些审批。

对话头部的 **NTR** 标签页显示 agent 的原始流：

- 计划和待办清单
- 每次工具调用的名称、状态、输出（默认折叠，点开看全部）
- 代码改动的 unified diff，带 `+N -M` 行数统计
- 用量读数

这个标签页是只读的：它不发消息、不取消任务、不启动进程。实时跟随，不需要手动刷新。

**主聊天区和 NTR 标签页的分工**：人和 agent 的对话在主聊天区，工具活动也按时间顺序内联在那里；NTR 标签页放主聊天区装不下的东西——计划、完整输出、diff、用量。

- **已接入的 NTR 智能体**：每个 agent 一行，标着进程状态。点开「展开配置与模型」看全部细节。
- **`★ 默认`**：新建 NTR 会话默认用哪个 agent。
- **每张 agent 卡片**：显示名、启动命令、npm 包名、环境变量、工作目录，全部直接摆在你面前，没有藏起来的默认值。
- **启动命令是一整行**：程序加参数，例如 `codebuddy --acp`。含空格的路径用引号包住。输入框下方会实时显示插件解析出的「程序 / 参数」。
- **测试按钮**：用当前表单里的值拉起一个一次性进程做握手，不保存、不注册。适合在改配置前先验证。
- **工作区目录**：agent 在哪个目录里干活。
- **对话中可见的模型**：agent 能报几百个模型时，这里挑你想在模型芯片菜单里看到的。没勾的仍然可用，只是不列出来。

在对话里起的 NTR 会话，工作目录就是你在这个 DSH 会话里选中的那个目录（侧栏点的那个）。对端 agent 的读文件、搜索、执行命令都在那里，它自己的进程也从那里启动。

有一类 agent 在进程启动那一刻就把工作区定死了，只改会话参数它不听。插件在它没有活动会话时会把它搬到新目录；有会话在进行时就保持原进程，不打断你的对话。

---

**会被平台风控吗？会封号吗？是反代吗？**

不会，也不是反代。dsh-ntr-plus 与 agent 之间的通信走 ACP——这是 agent 官方支持的协议入口。插件只负责启动你本地的 agent 进程并和它对话，全程不接触平台 API、不转发任何请求。模型调用由 agent 自己完成，跟你在终端里直接用它没有区别。在 NTR 提供的能力范围内合理使用，是官方允许的做法，不会因此封号。

**为什么选完 agent 之后，输入框里没看到 DSH 的模型选择器？**

那是设计如此。NTR 会话里，模型是 agent 自己的概念，所以那个位置换成了 NTR 底座。切回普通模式的会话，原生选择器就回来了。

**为什么首轮开始后，输入框行尾不显示 agent 名字了？**

一个会话一个 agent。首轮之前底座留着让你改选；首轮一开始，会话就锁在这个 agent 上，名字变成挂在输入框卡片上边缘的 `NTR · <agent>` 只读小挂牌。换 agent 会丢掉它这边的上下文，所以确认锁定后只能新建会话。模型、思考等级和高级配置芯片不受影响。首轮没有任何可见输出就失败/取消时，锁定会回滚，底座回来。

**锁定后想换 agent 怎么办？**

新建一个会话重新选。已锁定的会话不会接受 `session/chat-bind` 的改绑（宿主返回 `agent_locked`），这是刻意的：新 agent 没有这段对话的上下文，假装切换只会得到一段失忆的对话。首轮没有产生任何可见输出就失败的情况例外：锁定会自动回滚，可以直接重选。

**顶部看不到 NTR 标签页？**

每条会话都有这个标签页。这条会话还没绑过 agent 时，它是空的，会提示你去选一个。先在模式选择里选「NTR 模式」，再在 NTR 底座里选一个 agent。

**agent 卡住不动了？**

可以放心点停止。插件会取消这一轮，并在 agent 不理会取消时强制收尾，会话不会永久卡住。如果 agent 进程崩了，下次发消息会自动把它拉起来并回放上下文，历史不丢。

**agent 只回了一个空气泡？**

一部分 agent 会把上游失败（认证、计费、配额）当成「正常结束」。插件检测到这种情况时会补一条告警，不让失败静默。

**agent 没反应，也没报错？**

看设置页的测试按钮。它会在宿主侧跑一次完整的握手，把真正的错误（包括 stderr 尾部）显示出来。

**模型列表太长或太短？**

模型芯片的菜单没有搜索框，所以模型是**按需勾选**的。去设置页那张卡片里勾你想看的。不勾就没有那些条目，避免几百个模型刷屏。

**为什么 NTR 标签页里没有我发的消息？**

那个标签页只显示 agent 的原始流（它的计划、完整工具输出、diff、用量）。你和它的对话在主聊天区，工具活动按发生顺序内联在对话里。

**为什么输入框里多了一个下拉，里面的选项我没见过？**

那是 agent 自己的权限模式，选项文字由它下发。每个 agent 的叫法不一样，插件照原样列出。它管的是 agent 什么时候来问你，与 DSH 的「访问模式」无关。

**导入了 agent，但它的权限模式和别的 agent 不一样？**

正常。模式清单由每个 agent 自己声明（`session/set_mode` 下发），插件照原样列出，不统一翻译、也不补默认值。想改叫法要在 agent 自己的配置里改。

**从源码安装切到 npm / 市场版后，启用时报 `EPERM ... zod`？**

这是旧依赖残留，不是插件缺文件：错误路径里会出现 `node_modules/dsh-ntr-plus/node_modules/.pnpm/...`。源码安装用 `link:` 指向你的仓库；pnpm 的 hoisted 布局在切到 registry 版时会把包目录换成真实文件，但会留下链接目标里的 `node_modules`。这份旧树（旧版 `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` 及其失效的 `zod` 软链）会遮蔽新装的依赖，DSH 导入时 stat 到坏链就报 `EPERM`。处理：在插件管理器里卸载 `dsh-ntr-plus`，删除 `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/node_modules/dsh-ntr-plus`（或只删它下面的 `node_modules`），再重装并重启。桌面 App 的 profile 请直接在 App 的插件页卸载/重装，不要用命令行。

---

- **任意 ACP agent**：内置常见预设，也可以接入任何支持 stdio 的 ACP agent。自定义 agent 带「自定义」徽标。
- **多会话隔离**：多个会话可以同时跟不同 agent 对话，各自独立。
- **流式展示**：用户消息、agent 回复、思考过程、工具执行、任务计划都是流式的。
- **工具活动内联**：工具调用按发生顺序插进主聊天区，思考和回答分列它两侧，不分层。
- **真实权限**：agent 的权限模式原样列出，它的每次权限询问也原样呈现，你答什么它收到什么。
- **斜杠命令归 agent**：NTR 会话里 `/` 弹出的是 agent 自己声明的命令；DSH 的同名命令不会截走你的输入。
- **断线重连**：浏览器刷新或断网后，历史按序补齐。agent 进程崩了，下次发消息自动恢复。
- **空闲释放**：没有活动的 agent 进程会在空闲一段时候后自动退出，不占内存。有会话的进程不会被释放。
- **Windows 可用**：npm 全局安装的 agent 在 Windows 上也能正常启动和回收，不会残留后台进程。

以上是用户部分。以下写给要改这个插件、或要手工写配置文件的人。

在 Profile 层的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里挂载。省略 `cwd` / `allowedCwdRoots` 时用插件自有工作区 `~/.dsh/dsh-ntr-plus/workspaces`（保存时自动创建）；`command` 是**一整条命令行**，含空格的路径用引号包住。

```yaml
- id: dsh-ntr-plus
  name: dsh-ntr-plus
  config:
    agents:

可选的 agent 字段：`npmPackage`（PATH 里找不到时自动 `npm install -g`）、`exposedModels`（NTR 座位菜单列哪些变体）、`idleTimeoutMs`（聊天进程的空闲释放窗口，`0` = 永不释放，默认 30 分钟）、`mcpServers`（额外交给 agent 连接的 MCP 服务器）。插件级还有 `transcriptMaxEntries`（会话事件缓冲上限，默认 600）与 `probeModelsOnBoot`（保留字段，启动时已不再为每个 agent 探测，见 `bootstrapCatalogs` 的注释）。可靠性超时与重试的默认值（`startupTimeoutMs`、`cancelFallbackMs`、`staleCancelRetryDelayMs`、`staleCancelMaxRetries`、`permissionTimeoutMs` 与 `permissionFallbackTimeoutMs`）见 [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) 约束 12 与 13；设置页能改的都在设置页改。

`mcpServers` 是**插件自己的形状**（每条必带 `name` 与 `transport`），不是 ACP 线格式——线格式里 stdio 那条不带 `type`，照线格式手写会被 agent 静默丢弃：

```yaml
      - id: pi
        command: pi-acp
        mcpServers:
          - name: codegraph

这些服务器在**建会话时**交给 agent，由 agent 自己拉起并使用；agent 自己配置的 MCP 服务器不受影响，这里只是额外追加。

```bash
npm install          # 依赖
npm run build        # 宿主 TS 声明 + 浏览器 Bundle
npm test             # 测试套件
dsh plugin --profile web add ./   # 挂载到 Web Profile

以下每条都对应一处真实故障，改代码前先读对应文档。浏览器半区经 `/acp` RPC 与 `/api/acp/stream` SSE 和宿主半区通信；宿主半区每会话一个 `AgentBridge`，经 stdio JSON-RPC 驱动 agent 子进程。

代码位置：`src/index.ts`（插件入口）· `src/protocol.ts`（共享类型）· `src/impl.ts`（纯宿主逻辑）· `src/bridge.ts`（子进程通信桥）· `src/client/`（React 扩展）· `presets/acp/`（NTR 模式声明）· `~/.dsh/dsh-ntr-plus/`（运行时落盘）。

- **DSH 只出显示层**：插件不写 DSH 的模型路由，不接管宿主的模型目录，也不让 ACP 模型出现在 DSH 原生选择器里。
- **工作区即侧栏路径**：侧栏点开的目录必须成为 `session/new` 的 cwd **和** agent 子进程自己的 cwd。有一条 agent（codebuddy）在进程启动那一刻就定死工作区。
- **NTR 模式 = agent preset**：由 `presets/acp/acp.patch.yml` 随包声明，不挂工具、不注入项目指令、不做 compaction，让模型可见的表面完全属于对端 agent。
- **转发严格等于用户文本**：按 `source.kind === 'user'` 挑消息，不转发标题生成、compaction 这类辅助调用，也不拼任何边界叙述。
- **逐步切分 = 原生交错的工具卡**：一个 ACP turn 按工具活动切成多个宿主 step——段以 `tool-call` 卡收尾即结束本次 stream，宿主落定消息、执行卡（真实输出经 guard 虚拟工具应答）、续跑下一步；续跑段续读同一个仍在飞的 `session/prompt`，绝不新发 prompt。卡片因此夹在两个 assistant 节点之间，与原生多步对话一致。
- **绑定必须接到请求路径上**：guard 的 `agent/request` waterfall（`prepend: true`）把请求改写成绑定指向的 `acp/<agent>`，adapter 再做一次复查。
- **权限模式与审批是两层，都以 agent 为准**：`composer-mode.tsx` 的控件只渲染 agent 经 `session/set_mode` 下发的 `availableModes`，不写可见标签、不翻译选项名；`session/request_permission` 原样映射给用户。插件没有自己的权限开关：agent 问了就一定到人面前。早先那套由宿主替 agent 裁定的端口语义（`decidePermission`、fs 写栅栏）已删除，见 `docs/acp-convergence.md` §2.3。
- **跨平台路径**：`impl.ts` 不能 import `node:path`，绝对路径判定与 containment 全部手写，Windows 与 UNC 有专门用例。

Chat with any **ACP agent** (CodeBuddy, Pi, Oh My Pi, Claude Code, OpenCode, Qoder, …) right inside the web/desktop app of [DSH (DeepSeek Harness)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness), using the interface you already know.

**DSH provides the interface; the agent provides the capability.** The conversation list, composer, side panel, and message rendering all come from DSH; reasoning, tool execution, file access, and permission decisions all belong to the agent you configured — it runs in its own process, fully autonomous. This plugin does exactly one thing: wire the two sides together, and render the agent's output faithfully in DSH's UI.

> Model selection, thinking level, and work modes are **the agent's own concepts**, not DSH's model catalog. The plugin never swaps models for you, and never writes the agent's choices into DSH's global settings.

---

**NTR = Negotiated Target Routing.**

In one sentence: your host agent acts as an ACP client, negotiates capabilities and permissions with a target agent, and hands the turn over to it.

> **This release ships the prebuilt `lib/`**, so it works out of the box — see [INSTALL.md](./INSTALL.md).
> The "install from source" section below describes the upstream development flow and needs `tsconfig.json` and `tests/`, which this package does not include.

This package targets the plugin API of **DSH 0.1.5-rc through 0.2.x** (the browser half declares `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-*@0.1.5-rc.1`). Upstream 0.3.x reworked the permission pipeline and the model catalog, so **0.3.x is not supported** — the plugin may fail to load, or load but do nothing.

Two-step self check after installing:

This plugin is a DSH **bundle**: `package.json`'s `dsh.bundle.patch` declares the two patches shipped with the package — the plugin's own `cordis.patch.yml`, and the NTR-mode preset at `presets/acp/acp.patch.yml`. After `dsh plugin` installs it, the package joins the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` and the patch layers take effect **automatically** — no config file needs editing by hand.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:Feiyu180/dsh-ntr-plus
```

`--profile` is required (web: `web`, desktop app: `desktop`, TUI: `tui`). Restart DSH afterwards.

Download `dsh-ntr-plus-0.1.6.tgz` from the release, then:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-ntr-plus-0.1.6.tgz
```

This package already ships the built `lib/`; building is only needed if you change the sources, and that flow lives in the upstream repository (this package has no `tsconfig.json` / `tests/`).

> `dsh plugin` is a pnpm forwarder; `--profile <name>` is required. The official desktop app manages its own profile — do not run the CLI against it.

1. A working DSH install (web or desktop).
2. At least one ACP agent CLI. The plugin ships presets for common ones, and accepts any stdio-capable ACP agent.

1. Open **Settings → NTR**.
2. Pick a preset from the agent list to fill it in, or click "Create a custom agent from scratch" and type the launch command yourself.
3. Click **Test**. Success shows the agent's name and the handshake latency; failure shows an actionable error plus the tail of stderr.

After saving, the agent shows up in the NTR base at the end of the composer.

1. Create a conversation and pick **NTR mode** in the mode selector.
2. Pick an agent in the NTR base at the end of the composer.
3. Just talk.

The agent's replies and thinking appear in the main chat. Tool activity is interleaved in order: a line of `🛠️ **tool** · args`, with the output in a code block below. For full tool outputs, plans, and diffs, switch to the **NTR** tab in the conversation header.

---

Click it to choose which agent serves this conversation. The menu lists only agents — one control, one job. The agent's own model and thinking level are separate chips on the same row, each with its own menu; if the agent also publishes extra config options (temperature, provider toggles, …), an **Advanced** base appears to the left of the model chip, where you set them one by one. Before the first turn, the agent base sits pinned at the far right; once locked, it retires and model/thinking take over the right end. Those lists are reported by the agent itself — they are not your familiar DSH model list.
The base appears only in **NTR-mode** conversations. Normal conversations show DSH's native model selector.

**One conversation, one agent.** Until the first message is sent, the base stays put: pick, or change your mind freely. The moment the first turn **starts**, the conversation **locks** to that agent: the base collapses, and the name becomes a **small tag on the top edge of the composer card** (`NTR · <agent>`, straddling the edge) — display-only, not clickable. To switch agents, start a new conversation. The model, thinking-level, and Advanced chips stay in place; they belong to the same agent, so no context moves. If the first turn fails or is cancelled before producing any visible output, the lock rolls back automatically and the base returns for another pick.

Type `/` in an NTR conversation and what pops up is **the agent's own command list** — the ones it declares over ACP (e.g. `compact`, `session`, `model`), not DSH's. Selecting one just inserts the command name into the composer; pressing Enter sends the whole line to the agent as-is, and it executes it. The list works **before the first message**: the host remembers the commands this agent declared in its last session (an agent that has never run has to wait until after the first turn).

DSH's own `/model`, `/permission`, `/export`, etc. are **not** intercepted by the host in this mode: same-named commands go to the agent too, and the host's command menu and skill completions never appear. Slash behavior in normal conversations is unchanged.

readme.section: Approvals and the agent's own permission modes
readme.text:
When the agent wants to touch something sensitive, it asks you. The approval card shows up right in the chat composer; you click Allow or Deny, and it obeys.

Every agent asks differently: some offer a set of options, some only allow/deny, some attach the exact command they are about to run. The plugin presents these as-is, and never pre-decides for you.

readme.section: Approvals and the agent's own permission modes
readme.text: **Permission modes are defined by the agent.** Each agent puts its own mode list (e.g. `Always Ask`, `Accept Edits`, `Plan`, `Bypass Permissions`) in the composer's tool row; the option text is exactly what the agent sent. Switch a mode, and the agent decides accordingly when to ask you. The plugin adds no permission tier of its own, and doesn't translate mode names.

readme.section: Approvals and the agent's own permission modes
readme.text: > **Note**: DSH's own "Access mode" (read-only / workspace write / full) has no power over external agents. The agent lives in its own process; DSH's file sandbox can't reach it. What actually applies is the agent's own permission mode, plus the approvals it sends you.

The **NTR** tab in the conversation header shows the agent's raw stream:

- Plans and todo lists
- Every tool call's name, status, and output (collapsed by default; click to expand)
- Unified diffs of code changes, with `+N -M` line counts
- Usage readouts

The tab is read-only: it sends no messages, cancels no tasks, launches no processes. It follows live — no manual refresh.

**Division of labor between the main chat and the NTR tab**: your conversation with the agent lives in the main chat, and tool activity is inlined there in time order; the NTR tab holds what the main chat can't — plans, full outputs, diffs, usage.

- **Connected NTR agents**: one row per agent, with process status. Click "Expand config & models" for the full detail.
- **`★ Default`**: which agent new NTR conversations use by default.
- **Each agent card**: display name, launch command, npm package, environment variables, working directory — all in plain sight, no hidden defaults.
- **The launch command is one line**: program plus arguments, e.g. `codebuddy --acp`. Quote paths that contain spaces. Below the input, the plugin live-shows the program/arguments it parsed.
- **Test button**: launches a one-shot process with the current form values to do a handshake — nothing saved, nothing registered. Good for validating before you commit a config change.
- **Workspace directory**: the directory the agent works in.
- **Models visible in conversations**: when an agent reports hundreds of models, check here which ones appear in the model chip's menu. Unchecked ones still work; they're just not listed.

An NTR conversation started in chat uses the directory you selected in this DSH session (the one you clicked in the side panel) as its working directory. The agent's file reads, searches, and command execution all happen there; its process is also launched from there.

One class of agents pins the workspace the moment the process starts, and ignores session-parameter changes afterwards. The plugin relocates such an agent to the new directory when it has no active conversations; while conversations are live, it keeps the original process and doesn't interrupt you.

---
**Will the platform risk-control me? Will I get banned? Is this a reverse proxy?**

No, and it isn't a reverse proxy. dsh-ntr-plus talks to agents over ACP — the officially supported protocol entry point of those agents. The plugin only launches your local agent process and talks to it; it never touches platform APIs and forwards no requests. Model calls are made by the agent itself, no different from you using it directly in a terminal. Reasonable use within what NTR provides is officially allowed, and won't get you banned.

**Why is DSH's model selector gone from the composer after I pick an agent?**

By design. In NTR conversations, models are the agent's own concept, so that spot becomes the NTR base. Switch back to a normal-mode conversation, and the native selector returns.

**Why does the agent name at the composer's end disappear once the first turn starts?**

One conversation, one agent. Before the first turn, the base stays so you can change your pick; the moment the first turn starts, the conversation locks to that agent, and the name becomes the read-only `NTR · <agent>` tag on the top edge of the composer card. Switching agents would lose this side's context, so once locked, you must start a new conversation. The model, thinking-level, and advanced-config chips are unaffected. If the first turn fails or is cancelled with no visible output, the lock rolls back and the base returns.

**How do I switch agents after locking?**

Start a new conversation and pick again. A locked conversation refuses rebinding via `session/chat-bind` (the host returns `agent_locked`) — deliberately: the new agent has no context of this conversation, and a fake switch would only yield an amnesiac chat. One exception: if the first turn failed without producing any visible output, the lock auto-rolls-back, and you can re-pick directly.

**Can't see the NTR tab at the top?**

Every conversation has this tab. If the conversation has never been bound to an agent, it's empty and prompts you to pick one. First select "NTR mode" in the mode picker, then pick an agent in the NTR base.

**Agent stuck?**

Click Stop without worry. The plugin cancels the turn, and force-finalizes it if the agent ignores the cancel — a conversation never hangs forever. If the agent process crashed, the next message automatically brings it back up and replays the context; history survives.

**Agent replied with an empty bubble?**

Some agents treat upstream failures (auth, billing, quota) as "normal completion". When the plugin detects this, it appends a warning instead of letting the failure pass silently.

**Agent unresponsive, and no error either?**

Check the Test button in Settings. It runs a full handshake on the host side and surfaces the real error (including the tail of stderr).

**Model list too long or too short?**

The model chip's menu has no search box, so models are **opt-in**. Check the ones you want on that settings card. Unchecked ones simply don't appear, sparing you a wall of hundreds of models.

**Why don't my messages appear in the NTR tab?**

That tab shows only the agent's raw stream (its plans, full tool outputs, diffs, usage). Your conversation with it lives in the main chat, with tool activity inlined there in order.

**Why is there an extra dropdown in the composer, with options I've never seen?**

That's the agent's own permission mode; the option text comes straight from it. Each agent names them differently, and the plugin lists them verbatim. It governs when the agent asks you — unrelated to DSH's "Access mode".

**Imported an agent, and its permission modes differ from other agents'?**

Normal. Mode lists are declared by each agent itself (sent via `session/set_mode`); the plugin lists them verbatim — no unified translation, no defaults filled in. To change the wording, edit the agent's own config.

**Activation fails with `EPERM ... zod` after switching from the source install to npm / the market?**

That's stale dependency state, not a missing plugin file: the failing path will contain `node_modules/dsh-ntr-plus/node_modules/.pnpm/...`. The source install uses `link:` to your checkout; pnpm's hoisted layout replaces the package directory with the registry files but leaves the link target's `node_modules` behind. That old tree (an older `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` plus its broken `zod` symlink) shadows the freshly installed dependency, so DSH's import hits the bad link and fails with `EPERM`. Fix: uninstall `dsh-ntr-plus` in the plugin manager, remove `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/node_modules/dsh-ntr-plus` (or just its nested `node_modules`), then reinstall and restart. For the desktop app's profile, uninstall/reinstall from the app's Plugins page instead of the CLI.

- **Any ACP agent**: common presets built in, and any stdio-capable ACP agent works. Custom agents carry a "Custom" badge.
- **Multi-conversation isolation**: several conversations can talk to different agents at the same time, fully independent.
- **Streaming everything**: user messages, agent replies, thinking, tool execution, and task plans are all streamed.
- **Inlined tool activity**: tool calls are inserted into the main chat in the order they happened, with thinking and replies on either side — no layering.
- **Real permissions**: the agent's permission modes are listed verbatim, and every permission request is presented as-is. What you answer is what it receives.
- **Slash commands belong to the agent**: in NTR conversations, `/` pops the agent's own declared commands; DSH's same-named commands don't hijack your input.
- **Reconnect**: after a browser refresh or a network drop, history backfills in order. If the agent process crashed, the next message recovers it.
- **Idle release**: agent processes with no activity exit automatically after an idle window, freeing memory. Processes with live conversations are never released.
- **Windows works**: npm-globally-installed agent
That was the user part. What follows is for people modifying this plugin, or writing config files by hand.

Mount it in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. When `cwd` / `allowedCwdRoots` are omitted, the plugin's own workspace `~/.dsh/dsh-ntr-plus/workspaces` is used (created automatically on save); `command` is **one full command line** — quote paths that contain spaces.

```yaml
- id: dsh-ntr-plus
  name: dsh-ntr-plus
  config:
    agents:

Optional agent fields: `npmPackage` (auto `npm install -g` when not found on PATH), `exposedModels` (which variants the NTR seat menu lists), `idleTimeoutMs` (idle-release window for chat processes; `0` = never release, default 30 minutes), `mcpServers` (extra MCP servers handed to the agent). Plugin-level there are also `transcriptMaxEntries` (per-conversation event buffer cap, default 600) and `probeModelsOnBoot` (kept for compatibility; boot-time per-agent probing no longer happens — see the comment on `bootstrapCatalogs`). Reliability timeouts and retries (`startupTimeoutMs`, `cancelFallbackMs`, `staleCancelRetryDelayMs`, `staleCancelMaxRetries`, `permissionTimeoutMs`, `permissionFallbackTimeoutMs`) are covered by [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) constraints 12 and 13; anything editable in the Settings page should be edited there.

`mcpServers` uses the plugin's OWN shape (every entry carries a `name` and a `transport`), not the ACP wire shape — the wire's stdio entry has no `type`, and an entry written in the wire shape is silently dropped by the agent:

```yaml
      - id: pi
        command: pi-acp
        mcpServers:
          - name: codegraph
These servers are handed to the agent when a session is created; the agent launches and uses them itself. The MCP servers the agent configures for itself are unaffected — this only adds more.

```bash
npm install          # dependencies
npm run build        # host TS declarations + browser bundle

- **DSH renders, nothing more**: the plugin doesn't write DSH's model routing, doesn't take over the host's model catalog, and never lets ACP models appear in DSH's native selector.
- **Workspace = the side-panel path**: the directory opened in the side panel must become both the `session/new` cwd **and** the agent child's own cwd. One agent (codebuddy) pins its workspace at process startup.
- **NTR mode = an agent preset**: declared by `presets/acp/acp.patch.yml` shipped with the package — no tools, no injected project instructions, no compaction, so everything the model sees belongs to the remote agent.
- **Forwarding is strictly the user's text**: messages are picked by `source.kind === 'user'`; title generation, compaction, and other auxiliary calls aren't forwarded, and no boundary narration is ever spliced in.
